title: Eden Gardens | Kolkata Trips
description: Discover Eden Gardens Kolkata, India's iconic cricket stadium. Learn about its history, architecture, match tickets, timing, how to reach.
h1: Why Eden Gardens is Called the Mecca of Indian Cricket
textContent: Eden Gardens Eden Gardens Kolkata is much more than a cricket stadium—it is a symbol of India’s cricketing passion and one of the most celebrated sporting venues in the world. Located beside the sprawling Maidan in central Kolkata, this legendary stadium has witnessed unforgettable international matches, historic victories, and countless cricketing milestones. Known as the “Mecca of Indian Cricket,” Eden Gardens has been home to generations of passionate cricket fans since its establishment in the 19th century. Whether you’re visiting Kolkata for sightseeing or planning to watch an IPL or international match, Eden Gardens deserves a place on your itinerary. History of Eden Gardens Kolkata Eden Gardens was established in 1864, making it one of the oldest cricket stadiums in the world. The stadium derives its name from the nearby Eden Gardens, which were developed by the Eden sisters, Emily and Fanny Eden, during the British colonial period. Initially designed for cricket and other sporting events, the venue gradually evolved into India’s premier cricket stadium. Over the decades, it has hosted numerous memorable Test matches, One Day Internationals (ODIs), Twenty20 Internationals, IPL games, and major ICC tournaments. The stadium is the home ground of the Bengal Cricket Team and the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) in the Indian Premier League. Architecture and Design Eden Gardens combines historic charm with modern sporting infrastructure. Major features include: Seating capacity of approximately 66,000 spectators after renovation. Modern floodlighting system. International-standard dressing rooms. Advanced media and broadcasting facilities. Corporate hospitality boxes. Electronic scoreboards and giant LED screens. Excellent pitch and outfield maintained by the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB). Following extensive renovations before the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup, the stadium offers improved spectator comfort while preserving its historic identity. Memorable Matches at Eden Gardens Eden Gardens has witnessed some of cricket’s greatest moments, including: India vs Australia Test Match (2001) Perhaps the most famous Test in cricket history. VVS Laxman scored 281. Rahul Dravid scored 180. India followed on and won the match. Harbhajan Singh claimed India’s first Test hat-trick. ICC Cricket World Cup The stadium has hosted matches during: 1987 Cricket World Cup 1996 Cricket World Cup 2011 Cricket World Cup 2016 ICC World Twenty20 IPL Matches As the home of Kolkata Knight Riders, Eden Gardens regularly hosts packed IPL encounters featuring some of the world’s finest cricketers. Why Eden Gardens is Called the Mecca of Indian Cricket Several reasons make Eden Gardens legendary: Rich cricketing heritage Massive and passionate crowd Historic international matches Iconic atmosphere during IPL Home of Kolkata Knight Riders One of the oldest cricket grounds globally For cricket lovers, visiting Eden Gardens is comparable to visiting Lord’s Cricket Ground in England or the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia. Timings The stadium is generally not open for regular tourist visits. Visitors can access Eden Gardens: During international matches IPL matches Domestic cricket fixtures Special guided visits (occasionally organized) Public access depends on the event schedule. Entry Fees On Non-Match Days General tourist entry is usually not available. During Matches Ticket prices vary depending on: Tournament Seating category Hospitality package Match importance Tickets are usually sold online and through authorized counters before major matches. Best Time to Visit The ideal period to visit Eden Gardens is: October to March During these months: Pleasant weather Cricket season Domestic tournaments International fixtures IPL preparation (late winter and spring depending on the schedule) Watching a live match offers the best experience. How to Reach Eden Gardens By Metro Nearest metro stations include: Esplanade Maidan Both stations are within walking distance. By Bus Numerous government and private buses connect Eden Gardens with all major parts of Kolkata. By Taxi Yellow taxis and app-based cabs are readily available throughout the city. By Train The nearest railway station is Howrah Junction, approximately 5 km away. By Air From Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, the stadium is about 17 km away. Nearby Attractions A visit to Eden Gardens can easily be combined with several nearby landmarks: Maidan Victoria Memorial St. Paul’s Cathedral Princep Ghat Fort William Shaheed Minar Indian Museum These attractions are often included in a full-day Kolkata sightseeing itinerary. Visitor Tips Check the match schedule before planning your visit. Purchase tickets only through authorized sources. Arrive early on match days to avoid heavy traffic. Carry a valid photo ID if attending a match. Security checks are mandatory. Certain items such as large bags, power banks, and outside food may not be permitted during matches. Use public transport or the Metro on match days to avoid parking difficulties. Wear comfortable clothing and stay hydrated during day matches. Interesting Facts About Eden Gardens Established in 1864. One of the world’s oldest cricket stadiums. Nicknamed the Mecca of Indian Cricket. Home ground of the Kolkata Knight Riders. Managed by the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB). Hosted the famous India-Australia Test of 2001. Hosted multiple ICC World Cup tournaments. Located beside Kolkata’s historic Maidan. Why Visit Eden Gardens Kolkata? Even if you’re not attending a match, Eden Gardens remains an iconic landmark that reflects Kolkata’s deep love for cricket. Its rich sporting heritage, historic matches, and electric atmosphere make it one of the city’s most celebrated destinations. For cricket enthusiasts, experiencing a game here is often a once-in-a-lifetime memory. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Why is Eden Gardens famous? It is one of the world’s oldest cricket stadiums and is known as the “Mecca of Indian Cricket” because of its rich history and passionate fans. 2. When was Eden Gardens established? Eden Gardens was established in 1864. 3. Where is Eden Gardens located? It is located beside the Maidan in central Kolkata, West Bengal. 4. What is the seating capacity of Eden Gardens? The stadium currently accommodates approximately 66,000 spectators. 5. Which IPL team plays at Eden Gardens? The Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) use Eden Gardens as their home ground. 6. Can tourists visit Eden Gardens? General public access is limited. The stadium is primarily open during cricket matches and selected special events. 7. Which is the nearest Metro station? Maidan and Esplanade Metro stations are the closest. 8. What is the best time to visit Eden Gardens? October to March is the best period, especially if a cricket match is scheduled. 9. What was the most famous match played here? The India vs Australia Test in 2001, where India achieved a remarkable comeback victory after following on. 10. Is parking available? Limited parking is available during events, but public transport is recommended on match days. 11. Are guided tours available? Guided tours are not offered regularly and are usually limited to special occasions. 12. What attractions are close to Eden Gardens? Nearby attractions include the Maidan, Victoria Memorial, Princep Ghat, Fort William, St. Paul’s Cathedral, Shaheed Minar, and the Indian Museum. 13. Is photography allowed? Photography is generally permitted outside the stadium, while camera policies inside depend on the event and security regulations. 14. Can I buy tickets at the stadium? Tickets may be available at authorized counters for certain matches, but online booking is recommended for major fixtures. 15. Is Eden Gardens included in Kolkata city tours? Yes. Most Full-Day Kolkata City Tours include an exterior stop at Eden Gardens along with other iconic landmarks around the Maidan and colonial district.
